Hi Tom / Sara 

Thanks again for the call earlier  good discussion. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the next technical deep dive:

Summary from our call:
- FinSecure is evaluating Redwood for production inference across a couple of workloads (document classification + redaction pipeline).
- Primary concern: strong data isolation and assurance that customer data (input, KV cache, model context) does not leave FinSecure-controlled boundaries.
- Candidate deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pools, managed by Redwood), Private VPC / on-prem (customer-managed control plane).

Key clarifying questions (so our SE can prepare the right diagrams & controls):
1) Do you require the entire inference path (control plane and data plane) to reside in your VPC / on-prem, or is it acceptable for the control plane to be hosted by Redwood as long as the data plane (inference endpoints, storage, and keys) is within your VPC?
2) Are there specific certifications/regulatory constraints we should prioritize (PCI, SOC2, ISO27001, data residency) beyond what we discussed?
3) Do you anticipate needing HSM/KMS integration for key material (bring-your-own-key) for model inputs/outputs?

Next steps I propose:
- Nikhil (SE) to run a technical deep dive that includes network diagrams for Dedicated vs Private VPC, KMS/HSM options, and audit/logging options.
- I’ll send our SOC2 summary and a sample network diagram ahead of the call.
- Can we aim for a 60-minute deep dive next week? Please share 2 slots that work for your infra/security team.

Attachments: FinSecure_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (you sent during call)  I’ve attached to this thread for our internal tracking.

Marissa  thanks for the recap. Quick answers below and a couple of asks so we can prep on our side.

Answers:
- Our compliance requirement is that customer data at rest and in-transit for inference must be under our control. Ideally we'd prefer the inference endpoints and any persisted caches to live inside our VPC or on-prem.
- Regarding the control plane: we can accept a hosted control plane as long as there’s explicit network isolation for the data plane and AWS PrivateLink / VPC peering options for connectivity, plus detail on where logs/audit events are streamed and stored.
- We do need BYOK/KMS integration for keys. HSM would be a nice-to-have for later phases.

Regulatory scope: SOC2 is table stakes; we’re also subject to additional vendor risk checks for financial services (we’ll share the full questionnaire).

Asks for Redwood ahead of the deep dive:
1) Can you share a short diagram that shows the difference between Dedicated and Private VPC (control plane vs data plane) and where data resides for each?
2) Can you surface what logs/audit events are available, retention windows, and how they can be pushed to our logging pipeline (e.g., S3, Splunk, or a Kafka endpoint)?
3) Any sample text for contractual language around data isolation would be helpful (we may need to insert into vendor review).

Hi Tom / Sara 

Thanks  below are practical clarifications from an implementation perspective. I’ll cover these in more detail on the deep dive and bring network diagrams.

Short answers:
- Dedicated capacity: provides isolated GPU pools and tenant-level separation for compute. However, by default the Redwood control plane (management, routing, job orchestration) is hosted by Redwood. Data plane isolation options for Dedicated include private networking (VPC peering or PrivateLink) and dedicated storage buckets that we can lock down. In other words: compute and storage can be isolated, but the control plane will still be Redwood-managed unless you move to Private VPC.

- Private VPC / On-prem: full control-plane and data-plane residency inside your network. Redwood offers a private control plane deployment model (customer-managed control plane) or an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. This is the only option where we guarantee that control plane telemetry and orchestration do not transit Redwood-managed systems.

- Keys & encryption: we support BYOK via AWS KMS integration today (customer-provided KMS keys). HSM integrations are available through our professional services offering  we can scope that if you prefer hardware-backed keys.

- Logs & audit: we can stream audit logs (request/response metadata, per-request token counts, model/version identifiers) to customer-owned S3 or a Splunk/Kafka endpoint. Retention policies are configurable; we will provide default retention and options to archive logs to your long-term store.

What we’ll bring to the technical deep dive:
- Side-by-side network diagrams for Dedicated vs Private VPC (control plane vs data plane clearly marked).
- Sample contract language and SLR wording for data isolation and auditability.
- Redwood SOC2 summary and a brief on what evidence we can provide during vendor review.

I’ll attach a SOC2 summary and a sample network diagram to this thread for your review. Can we lock in Wed 3/3 11am PT for the deep dive? Marissa, please confirm with them  Vivek, FYI in case pricing/commitment questions come up.
